description.summary: privileged shell protocol for the Huginn compositor

protocol.description:
The contract between the Huginn compositor and the Muninn desktop shell.
This protocol covers only what no standard protocol provides. Panels, the dock and the wallpaper are wlr-layer-shell surfaces; the lock screen is ext-session-lock-v1. Do not duplicate those here.
The compositor should only advertise this global to clients it considers privileged. Huginn does not yet enforce that, which is tracked as a gap rather than a design decision.
Stability: additive changes only. Add requests and events and bump the interface version; never change or remove an existing one. Keeping to that is what makes moving this file to its own repository a mechanical step.

interface.name: raven_shell_manager_v1

description.summary: entry point for the desktop shell

interface.description: Handed to the shell so it can observe compositor state it cannot see as an ordinary Wayland client.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Objects created through this manager are unaffected and must be destroyed separately.

request.name: get_workspace_state
request.description:
Create an object reporting how many workspaces exist, which one is active, and which hold windows, so a panel can render indicators.
The compositor sends one state event immediately on creation, so a client never has to render a placeholder while it waits.

request.name: open_quick_settings

description.summary: open the compositor-drawn quick settings panel

request.description:
Open the quick settings panel, exactly as the keybinding would. The panel is drawn by the compositor, so a bar that wants a click on its battery to lead somewhere has to ask for it here; it has no surface of its own to show.
A no-op if the panel is already open, and while the session is locked: nothing resolves under the lock screen, and a request from a client is not an exception to that.

description.summary: workspace count, active index and occupancy

request.name: activate
request.description:
Ask the compositor to make workspace 'index' active.
An out-of-range index is ignored rather than clamped: clamping would turn a shell bug into a silent jump to an unrelated workspace, which is harder to notice than nothing happening.

event.name: state
event.description: Sent once when this object is created, and again whenever any field changes. The compositor does not send this event if nothing changed.

arg.name: active
arg.summary: zero-based index of the active workspace

arg.name: occupied
arg.summary: bitmask; bit N is set if workspace N holds at least one window. Caps at 32 workspaces, which is well beyond any sane count
